questoes.enunciado: Identify the specific subdivision indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The pars nervosa and the infundibulum form the neurohypophysis, which is derived from nervous tissue. As such, this subdivision is pale staining compared with the regions of the adenohypophysis seen on the right side of this section.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The infundibulum is a part of the neurohypophysis and forms the stalk that connects the entire pituitary to the ventral surface of the brain. The infundibulum is continuous with the pars nervosa and consists of axons from hypothalamic neurons which eventually terminate in the pars nervosa.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure(s) indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. These protein-filled spaces are remnants of the embryological structure called Rathke's pouch. Rathke's pouch is an evagination from the roof of the stomodeum and gives rise to all subdivisions of the adenohypophysis. The cells encompassing the cysts and located between these cysts and the pars nervosa comprise the pars intermedia.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This section is from the pars distalis of the pituitary and, thus, contains both basophils and acidophils. In this hematoxylin and eosin stained section, basophils are distinguished by the magenta-stained secretory granules in their cytoplasm. These cells are not related to the basophils present in blood.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This section is from the pars distalis of the pituitary and, thus, contains both acidophils and basophils. In this hematoxylin and eosin stained section, acidophils are distinguished by the pinkish-orange, eosin-stained secretory granules in their cytoplasm.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This Masson-stained section is from the pars distalis of the pituitary and, thus, contains both basophils and acidophils. The granules in the basophils stain a greenish-purple color. These cells are not related to the basophils present in blood.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This Masson-stained section is from the pars distalis of the pituitary and, thus, contains both basophils and acidophils. The granules in the acidophils stain bright orange with this stain.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Herring bodies are the expanded axon terminals of hypothalamic neurons. Herring bodies are most numerous in the pars nervosa and are eosinophilic with a granular appearance. They can vary in size, depending on the number of hormone-containing vesicles they contain. The nuclei adjacent to Herring bodies are those of pituicytes.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells whose nuclei are indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Pituicytes are modified astrocytes that are found throughout the infundibulum and pars nervosa. In addition to the Herring bodies, the other major structures seen in this section are the numerous, small-caliber axons of hypothalamic neurons.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The thyroid gland is composed of spherical follicles which are formed by a simple epithelium of follicle cells. The cavity of the follicle is filled with thyroglobulin which is secreted by the follicle cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Parafollicular or clear cells in the thyroid gland are located both in the interfollicular connective tissue and the follicle epithelium. These cells secrete calcitonin in response to elevated blood calcium levels.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region indicated by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The zona reticularis is the innermost region of the adrenal cortex, positioned between the zona fasciculata and the adrenal medulla. The cells of the zona reticularis are arranged in branching rows, thus appearing like a network or reticulum.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the "X's".

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Blood enters the adrenal gland through the capsule and percolates through the wide-diameter, fenestrated capillaries of the cortex. Steroid secretions of the cortical cells are released into these capillaries. Blood eventually exits the organ via veins located in the medulla.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the organ that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Like most endocrine organs, the principal cells of the parathyroid gland are arranged in plates or cords with large numbers of capillaries between them. The main distinguishing feature of the parathyroid gland is the presence of the large oxyphil cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Oxyphil cells are the minor cell type in the parathyroid gland. They are larger than the principal cells and have abundant cytoplasm that contains numerous mitochondria.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region indicated by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The zona glomerulosa is the outermost region of the adrenal cortex and lies between the capsule and the zona fasciculata. The cells of the zona glomerulosa are arranged in spherical clusters.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the region indicated by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The adrenal medulla forms the core of the adrenal gland and is composed of modified neurons called chromaffin cells. Large veins, also located in the medulla, drain blood from the entire gland.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In this horizontal section of the pituitary gland, the pars distalis is distinguished by its overall basophila compared with the pars nervosa above it. The pars intermedia occupies the region at the interface of these two major subdivisions. The pars distalis contains a mixture of basophils and acidophils, each with its distinctively staining secretory granules, not visible at this low magnification.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CORRECT.  The pars nervosa and the infundibulum form the neurohypophysis, which is derived from nervous tissue.  As such, this subdivision is pale staining compared with the regions of the adenohypophysis seen on the right side of this section.
